tagline.text: Step into the paintings on 15th Avenue, Cubao at this 3D trick-art museum

location.label: Location
location.text: 175 15th Avenue, Barangay Socorro, Cubao, Quezon City

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Year-round (a good indoor plan on rainy days)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱700~1,300 (one adult, including ticket, transport and snacks, half-day basis)

children.text: Art In Island is a 3D trick-art museum on 15th Avenue in Cubao, Quezon City. Stand at the marked spot in front of a painting on a wall or floor and take a photo, and it looks as if you have stepped into the scene. It is air-conditioned and indoors, so it works in any weather.

Art In Island is a 3D interactive art gallery in the Cubao area of Quezon City, Metro Manila. According to Wikipedia, it opened on December 25, 2014, and 18 Korean visual artists completed the first exhibits over about four months. The two-storey building covers about 3,800 square meters and holds more than 100 interactive works. The paintings use optical illusions to make flat walls and floors look three-dimensional, so instead of just looking at the art, you step into it and take photos. You will find reinterpretations of famous paintings, natural scenes such as the sea and waterfalls, and fairy-tale fantasy scenes.

This museum is a good place to catch your breath from the Philippines' hot, humid weather. The whole building is air-conditioned, so it is a comfortable break from the midday sun, and it also works as a backup plan when heavy rain hits in the wet season. It suits families with children, friends or couples who enjoy taking photos, and anyone who wants a light indoor outing in Manila for a day. Travelers who come for history or natural scenery should treat it as a short stop.

The focus here is on taking photos rather than quietly viewing art. Stickers or marks on the floor show the camera position and the spot where you should stand for the most convincing effect, and staff will tell you the best angle for each work if you ask. If you go alone, there may be nobody to take your photos, so going with a companion is recommended. There are reports that you can hire a photographer for solo visitors, but check on-site whether this is available and what it costs.

Operating details have changed often over time. The museum reportedly closed after the pandemic and reopened on December 15, 2022, and from April 2023 its hours changed to Tuesday to Sunday, opening at 11:00 AM. It also carries the subtitle Art In Island: The Media Square. Before you go, be sure to check the official Facebook page for whether it is open, the hours, and the prices.

blocks.title: 3D trick art you can step into

children.text: This is the heart of the museum. Stand at the marked spot in front of a painting drawn in perspective on a wall or floor, and the photo makes it look as if you are standing over a deep pit or sitting beside a waterfall. Don't take just one photo from the same spot; try several poses such as sitting, jumping and reaching out.

There are more than 100 works made by Korean visual artists, grouped by themes such as an undersea world, winter and Christmas, love and fantasy. In 2019 the museum was described as having 12 zones, but the current layout may have changed, so check the map on-site.
Wikipedia says some works are derived from famous paintings such as the Mona Lisa and The Scream. Because you step into a picture everyone knows, even children can enjoy it easily.

blocks.title: Media art show and central hall

children.text: A 2019 guide says a media art show is held in the central hall. It is a handy place to rest after the photo zones. Check on the day of your visit whether the show is running and when.

blocks.title: Photo points that staff will show you

children.text: Each work has a sticker on the floor marking where to stand, and staff will tell you from which angle to shoot if you ask. When taking photos of each other, hold the phone low, and the painting and the real person connect more naturally.
The building is cool with air-conditioning and you can spend 2–3 hours in one place, which helps when planning around midday heat or rain. It also makes a good rest stop in a full day of sightseeing.

blocks.title: Cubao Expo, with Korean restaurants and cafes nearby

children.text: After your visit, it is easy to continue to the restaurants and cafes around Cubao Expo (Cubao X). The Korean restaurant Jeongwon is described as next door, and the museum is also known to have a cafe inside. Check on-site whether they are open.

items.title: Afternoon half-day course
items.subtitle: The museum and a stroll around Cubao Expo

children.text: Arrive when it opens. On weekday mornings there are fewer people, so you can take photos without waiting long in front of the same work.
Take off your shoes at the entrance and go in wearing socks. If you have none, you can reportedly rent or buy slipper socks on-site (an earlier guide listed
Go around from the first zone in order and take photos at each photo spot. Ask staff for the best angle, and try three or four poses at each work.
Finish the tour, stop by the souvenir shop, and head out. A visit usually takes about
2–3 hours
Walk over to Cubao Expo for lunch or coffee. Opening times vary by shop, so some may still be closed before noon.
On Saturdays and Sundays tickets are sold until 7:00 PM, so you can also go in the late afternoon, but it is a crowded time, so weekdays are recommended.

items.title: Full-day Cubao course
items.subtitle: Trick art combined with Araneta City

children.text: Have an early lunch or brunch in Cubao, then head to the museum in time for opening.
Visit Art In Island. You will take many photos and your phone battery drains fast, so bring a power bank.
Browse the vintage shops and cafes at Cubao Expo. Some shops open in the late afternoon.
Move on to the nearby Araneta City malls and arena area and spend the time until dinner there.
Your trip home will overlap with rush-hour traffic, so getting a Grab may be difficult. Allow plenty of time.
This course is an example that groups nearby places together. Check each shop's opening hours on the day of your visit.
From Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL), take Grab or a taxi to Cubao. It is not close, and depending on traffic it can take more than
1 hour
, so leave extra time.
From downtown hotels such as Makati or BGC, Grab is also the easiest option. Set the destination to Cubao Expo (Cubao X) or Art In Island.
EDSA and the Cubao area are very congested around rush hour, so choose your departure time by checking traffic.
Fares vary greatly with time and demand, so no fixed amount is given here.
Get off at the Araneta City side of Cubao, where MRT-3 and LRT-2 meet.

According to two guides from 2017 and 2019, one route was to get off near Farmers Plaza, walk to the Rosario terminal next to the Smart Araneta Coliseum, take the Rosario-Citibank jeepney, and get off at 15th Avenue. Routes may have changed, so check on-site.
A route in through the back entrance of Cubao Expo is also described.
The address is 175 15th Avenue, Barangay Socorro, Cubao, Quezon City.
A route to the parking lot through Cubao Expo is described. Check parking fees and space on-site.
It is an indoor attraction, so you can visit year-round, and it is especially useful for avoiding rain in the June–November wet season or the midday heat of the dry season. Just avoid the crowds.
The quietest time is weekday mornings. On weekends, holidays, the year-end season and school vacations, lines get longer and you wait longer in front of each work.

You can book a hotel in Cubao, but most travelers stay in Makati or BGC and come by Grab. Cubao is convenient because MRT and LRT meet there, and Araneta City has malls and hotels, so it is a handy base if you want to spend the evening in this area.

For meals, the Korean restaurant Jeongwon right next to the museum is mentioned, and Cubao Expo is described as having restaurants such as Bellini's, Tacio's and Cubao X Brewery. Check before your visit whether they are open. Because the museum was made by Korean artists, a Korean restaurant next door is one of its distinguishing features.
You take your shoes off to go in, so be sure to bring socks. You can go barefoot or in slipper socks, but bringing your own is better.
There are guides advising a thin jacket, as the whole building is cool with air-conditioning.
To blend in with the paintings, bright, solid-colored clothes show up well in photos. Clothes with very busy patterns can look mixed up with the painting.
Fully charge your phone and camera and bring a power bank. Some guides also say Wi-Fi is free.
Taking photos of each other is the key, so go with at least two people. If you are alone, ask staff or inquire about the photographer service.
Tripods and selfie sticks are listed as prohibited, and it is best not to use flash. Pets and outside food are not allowed.
If one person stands in front of a painting for a long time, others have to wait. If people are waiting, take turns.
Online booking platforms sometimes sell tickets at discounted prices. Check the refund terms and whether a date and time are fixed before you buy.
Hours and admission prices change often and differ by source, so be sure to check the official Facebook page before you go to confirm that it is open.
The museum is described as closed on Mondays, but some accounts say it opens on holidays, so check especially around holidays.
Last admission is listed as 6:00 PM on weekdays and 7:00 PM on weekends. You cannot enter after closing, so go early.
You walk around in socks only, so walk slowly so you don't slip, and hold children's hands.
Do not touch or lean on the works or walls. If a painting is damaged, other visitors will find it hard to take photos too.
The Cubao area is crowded and traffic is heavy at rush hour, so leave plenty of time for the trip home and watch your phone and belongings.

A complex right next to the museum, with independent shops and cafes. You can get there on foot.
